messages.subject: userGWAS NA values in output
parts:
Hello!

Apologies if this is glaringly obvious, I am attempting a genomic SEM using the same sample of around 4,000 individuals using 3 separate GWAS, with around 6mill SNPs in each set. This has resulted in memory issues so have broken the data down by chromosome. I initially ran the addSNPs and userGWAS separately but have since tried the combined steps of userGWAS with and without the addSNPs output (Output = addSNPs and Output = NULL). For the first 100 SNPs, the following occurs: 


modelCh1<-"F1 =~ NA*Var1 + Var2 + Var3

F1 ~~1*F1

Var1 ~~ a*Var1

a > .01

F1~SNP"


sub1<-"F1~SNP"


SNPSE<-.005


#### Output = NULL


> GWASfactor_ch1<-userGWAS(covstruc = LDSCoutput, SNPs = pSumstats2, estimation = "DWLS",

+                       model =  modelCh1, modelchi = F, printwarn = T, sub = sub1, 

+                       SNPSE = SNPSE, parallel = T, Output = NULL)

[1] "Please note that an update was made to userGWAS on 11/21/19 so that it combines addSNPs and userGWAS."

Secondly, just wanted to see if anyone else was having problems with updated/newer versions of R?

messages.author: 3b39745f73eec779
messages.subject: Re: userGWAS NA values in output
parts:
HI 

so just to be clear did you get the NA's before the update or not?

if its not the update (which it could be) then its either the low sample size (4.000 is very low for LD score regression or genomicSEM) or something about the specific sumstat you are using. 

Things I would do to figure out whats going on would include: running the model wthout SNP to see if that does work (because if the model already causes problems then we may be looking at the wrong issue here) then I would move on too fitting the model for 1 SNP.

its much easier to help solve this if you save your R workspace for a trial run of say 10-100 SNPs and email it to us/me:

m.g.nivard [at] gmail.com 


Best,
Michel
